$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file.
tranche: R2 — cut the webapp off its database credentials (WIN-257 T8)
purpose: R2's clause is WIN-257 T8: 'webapp database credentials can be removed.'
It has never been met. `apps/webapp/app/services/database.server.ts` is
byte-identical to `v1`. This ledger records what R2 could prove, what it
found to be false, and what it deliberately did not build.
THE BRIEF'S FIRST INSTRUCTION WAS BUILT ON A CLAIM THAT IS FALSE HERE.
The brief said: fix `tenancy-prisma-only`, whose `to` pattern is
`node_modules/(@prisma/|prisma|@platos/tenancy-database)` and which
therefore cannot see `internal-packages/tenancy-database/dist/index.js`.
That was true on `v1` and it is NOT true on this base. T5 (83b61dc5, 'make
`tenancy-prisma-only` able to see the door it names') is an ancestor of
5b236cdb — verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` — and the rule now
carries both spellings. Run rather than read:
$ node scripts/arch/arch-boundaries.mjs --scan-root apps/webapp
10 boundary violation(s).
All ten are `tenancy-prisma-only`. The rule the brief sent R2 to repair was
already repaired, and it fires on every webapp file that holds the import.
THE RULE THAT COULD NOT SEE ITS OWN TARGET WAS THE OTHER ONE.
`webapp-no-prisma` — the only rule in the set written FOR this cutover,
whose comment calls itself 'the M2.2 migration lock' — fired ZERO times on
those same ten edges. `arch-boundaries.mjs` does not resolve modules:
`resolveTargetVirtualPath` maps a non-alias bare specifier to
`node_modules/<specifier>` verbatim, so the webapp's import of
`@platos/tenancy-database` reaches the rule as
`node_modules/@platos/tenancy-database`, and the rule's `to` side spelled
only `node_modules/@prisma/` and two `internal-packages/` directories. The
one spelling it carried is the one the webapp has never used.
CREDIT, BECAUSE OVERCLAIMING A FIND IS ITS OWN DEFECT. T5 SAW THIS. Its
ledger says, in its own words: '`webapp-no-prisma` — whose `to` pattern
DOES carry the workspace path — reports 0, because it cannot see the
specifier form. Each rule was blind to the half of the shape the other
could see.' T5 fixed the half its clause covered and left this one, because
its remaining clause was the scan root and the scan root belongs to the
cutover. R2 closes the other half. The figures differ by one and both are
right: T5 measured `--scan-root apps/webapp/app` and got 9; R2 measures
`--scan-root apps/webapp`, which also reaches
`test/authenticatedOrganizationRouteEvidence.test.ts`, and gets 10.
WHY THE CUTOVER ITSELF IS NOT IN THIS BRANCH, AND WHY THAT IS NOT BUDGET.
The surface reproduces exactly as the brief states: 15 operations in 11
files, measured independently by `webapp-prisma-surface.mjs` through the
TypeScript parser — 12 `database.<model>.<op>(` call sites, 1
`database.$transaction`, and 2 model operations on that transaction's own
callback parameter. The brief's rejection of the issue's '~117' also
reproduces, and the split is exact rather than approximate: 122 textual
`database.` references in `apps/webapp`, of which 98 are under
`apps/webapp/test/` — `vi.mock` factories and the assertions against them,
which migrate by DELETION — and 24 under `apps/webapp/app/`. A gate pinned
to the text figure would have been arguing with itself from its first run.
Every one of those 15 needs a REST endpoint, and NONE of them exists.
`apps/core-api/src/transports` at 5b236cdb holds the chassis, `envelope`,
`fault`, `page`, `transport-errors`, and `apps/core-api/src/http` holds a
health controller and a not-found controller. There is no route that reads
or writes tenancy state. The frozen `origin/main` oracle's 300-row REST
surface has no organization, project, environment, environment-variable or
end-user route either, so these endpoints are NEW — they are R1's, not a
surface R2 could have joined to.
R1 LANDED WHILE THIS BRANCH WAS BEING GATED, and the honest reading changed
with it. `origin/tejas/win-267-r1-identity-rest` @ c98b5309 is the identity
and tenancy REST surface, and it is EIGHT routes:
GET    /api/v1/identity/session
POST   /api/v1/bff/session
DELETE /api/v1/bff/session
GET    /api/v1/organizations
POST   /api/v1/organizations
GET    /api/v1/projects
POST   /api/v1/projects
GET    /api/v1/environments/:environmentId/end-users
Read off the controllers on that branch, not inferred from its title. Held
against the 15 + 2, they cover NINE outright — the two organization reads,
the organization create, the project read, and the whole of `projects.new`
(`POST /projects` commits the project, its first environment and the
creator's ADMIN membership in one unit of work, so the `$transaction`, both
of its creates and the loader's membership pre-check all go), plus
`authorizeOperatorSession` through `GET /identity/session`.
TWO MORE HAVE A ROUTE THEY CANNOT REACH. `GET /environments/:environmentId/
end-users` takes an environment ID. The webapp has three SLUGS. Nothing on
R1's surface resolves (organizationSlug, projectSlug, environmentSlug) to an
environment id: `ProjectResource` is id, organizationId, slug, name,
archivedAt, createdAt and `through`, and carries no environments. So
`endUser.findMany` and `endUser.count` are blocked on the SAME missing route
as `auth.server.ts`.
SIX HAVE NO ROUTE AT ALL: the environment lookup by slug and
`authorizeEnvironmentOperator` (both `auth.server.ts`, and between them the
gate for every scoped route the dashboard has), the two environment-variable
operations, and the organization-with-memberships read that
`settings.team` needs. 9 covered + 2 blocked + 6 absent = 17.
This is R2 saying so rather than inventing a second surface, which is what
the brief asks for in exactly this case. The three enum-only importers
(`ProjectRole`, `OrganizationRole`, `EnvironmentVariableKind`) could have
been moved to a shared contract without any endpoint, which would have
dropped the gate's violation count while every one of the 15 credentialed
operations still ran. That is a green gate over an unchanged credential, and
it was declined rather than banked.
AND THE FIGURE IS 17, NOT 15. The brief's 15 is exactly right about what it
counts, and it does not count the client HANDED to a callee rather than
called on: `new PlatosAuthService(database, …)` and
`authorizeEnvironmentOperator(database, …)`, both in `auth.server.ts`, both
the authentication path. Neither is `database.<model>.<op>(`, neither is a
`$transaction`, and a gate that reached zero without counting them would
certify a webapp that still holds a live client and still authenticates
every request through it. `clientHandOffs` counts them and they are part of
`cutoverComplete`.
WHAT IS ENFORCED INSTEAD IS THE RATCHET, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.
`webapp-prisma-surface.mjs` measures the surface from the tree and ties it
to the two physical facts that constitute the clause — whether
`database.server.ts` exists, and whether `DATABASE_URL` is still a required
boot credential. A tree with the file deleted and the surface still present
fails. A tree with the surface gone and the credential still mandatory
fails. A completed cutover that does not switch `apps/webapp` into
`DEFAULT_SCAN_ROOTS` fails. Neither half of the clause can be declared done
in prose while the other half sits still.
NOTHING IN THIS LEDGER NEEDS A DATABASE, A CONTAINER OR A DOCKER DAEMON.
Every entry is a file edit plus one `node --test` process.
procedure: Each entry names one edit, the command that judges it, and the NAMED test
cases that go red. `killCount` counts distinct `it(...)` cases, not
assertions and not suite roll-ups. After each entry the file is restored
from a byte copy and the command re-run to exit 0, so a kill is never a
leftover from the entry before it.

declared.name: the cutover itself — routing the 15 operations through core-api and deleting `database.server.ts`
declared.tried: Enumerating every one of the 15 operations, and the 2 client hand-offs the 15 does not count, against the endpoints available to receive them — first on this base, then against `origin/tejas/win-267-r1-identity-rest` @ c98b5309 once it appeared.
declared.result: NOT BUILT, and named rather than partially done. R1's eight routes cover 9 of the 17, leave 2 with a route they cannot reach for want of a slug-to-environment-id resolution, and leave 6 with no route at all — including `authorizeEnvironmentOperator` and the environment lookup, which together gate EVERY scoped route in the dashboard. Cutting the 9 alone would leave `database.server.ts` in the tree, `DATABASE_URL` required at boot and a live `PrismaClient` authenticating every request: the clause's own words would still be false and the gate would read better.
declared.why-unfalsifiable: A mutation entry needs a guard to break. There is no code here to break, because a partial cutover is a worse tree than no cutover — it retires the calls a reviewer can see and leaves the credential a reviewer cannot. What IS falsifiable is that the tree has not been declared done: `evaluate` refuses a zero surface while the module or the credential stands, and M05, M06 and M09 kill each half of that refusal separately.
declared.measured: 17 = 15 + 2, listed call site by call site with file and line by `webapp-prisma-surface.mjs --report`. R1's eight routes read off its controllers at c98b5309.

declared.name: moving the three enum-only imports out of `@platos/tenancy-database`
declared.tried: `ProjectRole`, `OrganizationRole` and `EnvironmentVariableKind` are compile-time constants. Re-exporting them from a contract package would need no endpoint at all and would drop `clientImporters` from 10 toward 6.
declared.result: DECLINED. It moves the gate's number without moving the credential: all 15 operations would still run against a live `PrismaClient` built from `DATABASE_URL`. A green count over an unchanged credential is worse than a red one, because the red one is true.
declared.why-unfalsifiable: This is a decision, not a guard. It is recorded here so that a later reviewer sees it was considered and refused rather than overlooked.
declared.measured: 6 of the 10 client importers hold ONLY enum or type imports; 4 hold the client itself or its auth surface.

declared.name: booting the webapp with no database credential in the environment
declared.tried: The brief asks for the webapp to boot and serve its routes with `DATABASE_URL` absent, to catch a lazily-imported module that only explodes on a request nobody sent.
declared.result: NOT RUN, because on this tree it cannot pass and running it would prove nothing new. `apps/webapp/app/env.server.ts` parses its schema at module scope with `DATABASE_URL: z.string().min(1)` — no `.default(`, no `.optional()` — so the process throws during import, before any route is reached. The static equivalent IS asserted: a case reads that schema line off disk and fails if it ever acquires a default or becomes optional, and `evaluate` refuses any tree in which the surface has reached zero while that line still exists.
declared.why-unfalsifiable: The dynamic proof belongs to the commit that lands the cutover, where it can pass. Asserting it here would mean asserting a failure, and a test that passes because the system is broken is the shape that survives the repair and then means nothing.
